I've sent the report to the coordinator. The parity battery is finished: 128 cases record from the current build and pass against themselves with a largest error of 3e-16.

  • Detection: a 1e-8 change to one input, or to the output of a core function, makes the affected cases fail. A 1e-12 change passes, as intended at the default tolerance (rtol 1e-10). A case that disappears, newly raises, or stops raising its recorded exception also fails with exit code 1.
  • Thread count: single-threaded runs are bit-identical. At 4 threads, results differ by up to 6e-16 run to run and by up to 2.1e-15 from single-threaded. That is far below the tolerance.
  • Wigner 3j at large j: the expected change is isolated in 10 wigner3j_large_* cases. Check it with --only 'wigner3j_large_*' -v. The current build is already slightly off there: the normalization sum at j = 100 is short by 1.1e-13.
  • Not covered:
    • io.mesh_spheres is not covered because gmsh isn't installed.
    • The support catalog is not covered because its embedded source hash changes on every edit.
    • A handful of private native functions that the public API never calls are left out.
    • The advect, jax and torch adapters are only sampled.
  • Main repo changed during the run: someone else rebuilt the main-tree extension at […] with uncommitted Cargo.toml changes (a faster dev build profile). I didn't make those edits. The baseline still passes against that rebuild, and single-threaded results are bit-identical, so it remains valid.
  • Runtime: a full compare takes 25–37 s on the original debug build and about 7–9 s on the rebuilt one.

Each worktree needs its own freshly built _native*.so, and compare prints which build it imported so engineers can confirm they tested their own.
